targets.title: How learning a musical instrument affects the development of skills.
targets.evidence_quote: Due to past inconsistencies in findings on musical participation and skill development and the complexity of background variables in this context, the present study aimed to replicate some of the findings by Hille and Schupp (2015) based on an extended data set that has been accumulated over the last decade.
targets.outcome_quote: Contrary to the precursor study, our main results indicate a long-term association with cognitive skills, but not with academic achievement. Further, our analyses suggest that openness, conscientiousness, and perceived control are all positively associated with musical participation, thus corroborating and expanding previous findings (e.g., Corrigall et al., 2013).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly contrast cognitive and achievement findings with the precursor while corroborating personality findings; the broad positive-association statement does not explicitly judge the replication as a whole.

reasoning: An extended SOEP panel adds observations to re-test the published study; coded as replication using a different, expanded sample. Title, authors and article boundaries verified in accepted manuscript; references included.
